title: 1989 AMC 8 Problem 14
statement: When placing each of the digits \(2,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(9\) in exactly one of the boxes of this subtraction problem, what is the smallest difference that is possible?

solutions.text:
The difference is smallest when the three-digit number (the top) is as small as possible and the two-digit number (subtracted) is as large as possible.

The largest two-digit number is \(96,\) using the digits \(9\) and \(6.\) The smallest three-digit number from the remaining digits \(2,\) \(4,\) \(5\) is \(245.\) So the smallest difference is \(245 - 96 = 149.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C .
hints: Make the three-digit number as small as possible and the two-digit number as large as possible
The largest two-digit number from these digits uses \(9\) and \(6;\) build the smallest three-digit number from the digits that remain
